messages:
jenny_support: Hey team — billing flagged a huge token delta for customer acct ACCT-442 (invoice inv_2026_03_01). Dashboard shows ~1.1M tokens for the period but invoice is charging ~3.2M. Customer says they only used streaming SSE chat with frequent client cancels/reconnects. Can we triage?

alex_billing: Thanks Jenny. Do we have the invoice id + affected request IDs or a sample timeframe? Also any user-visible request IDs (X-Request-ID) would help match logs.

jenny_support: Invoice inv_2026_03_01, window 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z -> 2026-03-01T23:59:59Z. Customer supplied one example session: session_id s-9f3b, request id x-req-77a3. They said flow is: client starts stream, gets a few deltas, client calls cancel (disconnect) then immediately opens a new stream to resume. They attached a trimmed SSE transcript: 
```
data: {"type":"delta","text":"Hello","token_count":5}
data: {"type":"delta","text":" world","token_count":3}
<client disconnect>
data: {"type":"final","text":"Hello world","token_count":50}
```
Customer says they saw the final chunk arrive briefly after they disconnected and then the duplicate token finalization shows up on invoice.

kofi_sre: Hmm. Two quick asks: 1) can you paste the exact SSE events (including any keepalive/ping frames) and client disconnect TCP FIN logs? 2) server side: full request lifecycle logs around x-req-77a3 (start, cancel, finalize). Usually token finalization happens when the runtime emits a terminal event. If the final event is emitted after the client disconnects, billing may still count it. There used to be an edge case where concurrent reconnects could trigger a second finalization for the same logical generation if the proxy replayed buffered output.

maria_support: Customer also attached their client code snippet. They do a hard socket close then immediately start a new POST to /v1/generate with the same conversation id. Posting their minimal repro: 
```bash
# client side repro (js pseudo)
fetch('/v1/generate?stream=true', {method: 'POST', body: prompt})
  .then(ev => { /* stream handling */ })
  .catch(() => {/* on error we abort and immediately retry */})
// they call controller.abort() then create a brand new fetch() within ~200ms
```

jenny_support: Attached server logs for x-req-77a3 (trimmed): 
```
2026-03-01T12:04:11Z INFO start req=x-req-77a3 session=s-9f3b
2026-03-01T12:04:12Z DEBUG stream chunk emitted tokens=8
2026-03-01T12:04:12Z INFO client disconnect detected (FIN)
2026-03-01T12:04:12Z WARN stream not yet finalized, scheduling finalize task
2026-03-01T12:04:12Z INFO finalize emitted final tokens=50
2026-03-01T12:04:12Z INFO finalize ack recorded
```

kofi_sre: That log sequence is exactly what I wanted to see. Two things: the "scheduling finalize task" is the runtime trying to flush remaining KV cache and produce a terminal chunk. If the client reconnects and issues a new request that races with the finalize task, our metering worker historically could double-count the finalization if both the old finalize and the new request caused separate billable token tallies before a de-dup check completed. There's an open bug (INF-1226) where immediate reconnect within the same session id + overlapping seq can produce duplicate finalization entries.

alex_billing: If that's the bug, ledger shows two separate events: one finalization event at 12:04:12 and another tied to the new request at 12:04:12. The invoice aggregator didn't dedupe because they had distinct internal stream IDs. We should: 1) confirm duplication in the billing ledger for that account and timeframe, 2) issue a corrective credit if confirmed, 3) patch or rollback the dedupe window.

maria_support: Agreed. Customer wants a quick explanation + credit while SRE investigates. Jenny, can you ask them for a second sample where they intentionally wait 1s before reconnecting to prove the delta goes away? Also ask for client-side TCP timestamps so we can correlate.

jenny_support: Sent back to customer with repro suggestion. They replied willing to test. Meanwhile I pulled a ledger diff for acct ACCT-442 and see two finalize entries at 12:04:12 for ~50 tokens each (total ~100) for this session; the invoice discrepancy is mostly many repeated quick reconnects across dozens of sessions — that multiplies.

kofi_sre: Next steps from my side: I'll run a local repro using the customer's snippet and our current runtime image. If I can reproduce, I'll open a hotfix PR to extend the de-duplication window and ensure finalize tasks are idempotent when a new stream starts with the same conversation id. If not reproducible, we'll instrument additional tracing to capture internal stream ids and ledger event IDs.

alex_billing: I'm going to create a billing ticket to credit the visible duplicates for this invoice as interim relief and mark it as reversible if SRE finds they were actually distinct legitimate billable events.

billing-bot: Invoice inv_2026_03_01 credit request created: ticket BILL-6091 by alex_billing (status: pending review).

maria_support: Thanks — please keep the customer updated. Quick note: add a KB blurb about "streaming reconnects and billing" so support can triage faster.

jenny_support: Will do. I'll follow up after the customer's 1s-wait test and post results here. :ear:
